title: Social Network Connectivity Analysis
scenario: You are managing a professional networking platform. Analyze the 'RequestAccepted' logs to identify the user who holds the highest number of unique connections. A connection is established when either a request is sent by an requester or received by an accepter. Determine the user ID with the maximum total connections and the corresponding count of those connections.
tableSchema: RequestAccepted (requester_id INT, accepter_id INT, accept_date DATE)
hint: Since connections are bidirectional, combine requester_id and accepter_id into a single stream using UNION ALL, then aggregate the counts per ID and select the record with the maximum total.
correctQuery: WITH AllConnections AS (SELECT requester_id AS id FROM RequestAccepted UNION ALL SELECT accepter_id AS id FROM RequestAccepted), ConnectionCounts AS (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS num FROM AllConnections GROUP BY id) SELECT id, num FROM ConnectionCounts ORDER BY num DESC LIMIT 1;
